title: Forms that survive real editing
outcome: Handle validation, dirty state, unsaved changes, and server conflicts without losing user work.
benefits: Fewer lost edits and more understandable failures.
drawbacks: Dirty-state and conflict handling require product decisions.
version: Modern JavaScript / TypeScript · Vue 3.5 where applicable · browser APIs
cue: A failed save should lose the request, not the work.

trace.title: Owned draft
trace.detail: A form is a small state machine: pristine, editing, validating, saving, saved, or failed. Some checks are immediate, such as a required title. Others depend on the server. Avoid showing aggressive errors before a user has had a reasonable chance to enter a value.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Type → dirty draft → client checks → request with expected version → server validation/authorization → success or conflict → keep or reconcile draft. An old successful response must not overwrite newer edits typed during the request.

Test paste, keyboard submit, double-click, slow save, field rejection, network loss, and record replacement. Use a visible saving status and a clear retry path.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Resetting from props on every server refresh can wipe a dirty draft. Sending the whole entity can include server-owned fields. A stale response can erase a newer edit.
